summary: Reviewed the two modified files: DeepLTestScreen.php (makeError → makeDangerous fix) and phpstan-result.txt (updated baseline).

The makeError() → makeDangerous() substitution at line 109 is correct. UI_Page_Section::makeDangerous() confirmed at Section.php:102. Danger styling is semantically appropriate for an error display path. No regression risk — the path is only exercised on a caught Translator_Exception_Request.

phpstan-result.txt baseline is accurate: 6 pre-existing errors in unrelated files (BaseDBRecordRequestType, FetchMany, PropertiesGrid, Submode, frame.footer, DisposingTest). DeepLTestScreen error correctly absent.

Code structure of DeepLTestScreen is clean. try/catch in handleTest() is properly scoped, early-return on error, success path follows. Admin screen patterns match framework conventions. No security concerns — form values go through the framework's getFormValues() before reaching the DeepL translator.

comments.note: DeepLTestScreen.php: handleTest() calls AppFactory::createDeeplHelper() directly (line ~96) to create the translator, rather than using the already-assigned $this->helper set in _handleActions(). This creates two DeeplHelper instances per form submission. Pre-existing code smell, not introduced by WP-006. Low impact — factory calls likely cheap — but worth a future cleanup pass.

No blocking issues found. The WP-006 changes are minimal, targeted, and correct. The makeError() → makeDangerous() fix is the only substantive code change and it improves code quality by removing a previously-silent incorrect API call.

phpstan-result.txt baseline management: the implementation agent surfaced that this file drifted from reality because it was not updated alongside commit d5da98fb. Consider adding phpstan-result.txt to the repository's CI or pre-commit awareness so drift is caught earlier.
